headline: Requires the State Department to add more detail on international adoption barriers to its yearly report to Congress.
what_it_does: The law changes what the Department of State must include in its annual report to Congress on intercountry adoptions. The report must now list countries whose laws block or ban adoptions by American parents, along with details about those bans. It must also describe steps the State Department has taken to help those countries reopen adoptions. Finally, it must assess how certain fees affect families adopting international children, sibling groups, or children with disabilities.

who_it_affects.group: American families seeking to adopt children from other countries
who_it_affects.how: The yearly reports to Congress will include more information about countries that block adoptions and about fees that may affect their costs.

who_it_affects.group: Children waiting for international adoption, including sibling groups and children with disabilities
who_it_affects.how: The reports will assess how certain fees affect adoptions for these children, which may draw attention to barriers they face.

who_it_affects.group: State Department staff who prepare the annual intercountry adoption report
who_it_affects.how: They must add new sections covering country bans, steps taken to reopen adoptions, and fee impacts.

when_it_takes_effect: Took effect on enactment, October 30, 2020; the expanded content applies to the State Department's annual reports going forward.
